transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because after my late shifts, I’ll get food and then keep eating once I’m home. Like a whole takeout meal, then chips, sweets, whatever’s around. Afterwards I look at it and I’m honestly shocked by how much I ate.
When this happens, do you feel unable to stop eating or control how much you’re eating?
Yeah. Once I start, it feels like I’m watching myself from the outside. I’m telling myself to stop, to put the food away, but I just keep opening containers and eating until it’s all gone.
After these eating episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit?
Sometimes, yeah. After I eat all that takeout and snacks, I’ll go to the bathroom and make myself throw up. I just… don’t want it sitting in me and turning into weight.
How often do you make yourself vomit after these eating episodes?
Sometimes—mostly after I’ve had a lot of takeout or snacks. I’ll go to the bathroom and make myself throw up because I’m worried it’ll turn into weight.
About how often do you make yourself vomit after these eating episodes?
Sometimes, after I get home and I’ve eaten too much takeout or snacks. I’ll make myself throw up because I’m scared it’ll turn into weight.
In a typical week, on how many days do you make yourself throw up after one of these eating episodes?
Usually one or two days in a week, I guess. It’s mostly when I’ve had a lot of takeout or snacks after work.
How much does your body shape or weight affect how you feel about yourself?
I’m not sure how much it affects me, exactly. I mean, I do worry about gaining weight sometimes, but I haven’t really thought about it in terms of how I feel about myself overall.
Have these binge-eating episodes with vomiting been happening for at least three months?

Yeah, I think so. Since I got settled after moving apartments, it’s been most weeks—at least one late-night time where I eat way more than I meant to, then try to make up for it by throwing up, skipping breakfast, or going for a long run.
Does your body shape or weight have a big effect on how you feel about yourself?
I don’t know if I’d say it has a big effect. I notice my weight and I can get bothered by it, but I haven’t really connected it to my overall self-worth.
Are you currently at a significantly low body weight for your height?
I’m not really sure what counts as significantly low. I haven’t noticed myself being especially underweight, though.
In a typical week, on how many days do you have one of these out-of-control eating episodes?
Most weeks, at least one day. It’s usually late at night.
After these eating episodes, do you ever use laxatives or diuretics to try to prevent weight gain?
Not laxatives or diuretics. Sometimes, after I get home and eat too much takeout or snacks, I make myself throw up so it won’t turn into weight.
Do your body shape or weight strongly affect how you feel about yourself as a person?
I’m not sure. I do worry about my weight sometimes, but I wouldn’t say it completely determines how I feel about myself.
During one of these episodes, do you eat an amount of food that most people would consider unusually large for a similar situation?
Yes. After a late shift, I might get a full takeout meal, then keep eating chips, sweets—whatever’s at home. By the end, I’m kind of shocked by how much I’ve had.
Do these eating episodes cause you a lot of distress?

Yeah, it does. I’m still showing up for work, but I’ve started avoiding after-shift meals with coworkers. And my mornings end up being about trying to undo the night before instead of resting or getting errands done.
Besides vomiting, do you regularly do anything else to try to prevent weight gain after these episodes, such as fasting or exercising for a long time?
Yeah. The next morning I’ll either run extra miles on the trail or skip breakfast before my shift, even if I’m exhausted. It feels like I have to make up for what I ate.
Would you say your body shape or weight has a major effect on how you feel about yourself as a person?
I’m not really sure how to answer that. I know I worry about it sometimes, but I haven’t really thought about whether it affects how I feel about myself overall.
When your weight goes up even a little, do you feel much worse about yourself as a person?

Yeah, I do. Even if it’s just a pound, or my pants feel a little tighter, I get really panicky. People at the venue tell me I look too lean, but I still worry guests or coworkers will notice and think I’ve let myself go.
